questions.question:

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

3, 13, 31, ?, 91
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The first step in solving a number series question *usually* is ***calculating the difference between the consecutive terms.***
 
• If the first set of differences are not adequate to identify a pattern, one should calculate the second set of differences

**Explanation:**__

The pattern followed here is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf578d6f408493195a1ea08333b2ea212f685b9e65e1c21596e1a3394bfc82bd.png] 

Hence, the number that will complete the series is **57**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

__
 
• **There are multiple ways of solving the given question. **
 
• Two more methods are shown below:

**Method I**__**:**

Each term of the given series can be expressed as "***a × (a + 1) + 1"*** as shown below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb70b224ce5b301222d4ed2d9e9874437dd4fd93790c7342fb8ca8cf8f64b1d3.png] 

Among the given options, ***only 57 can satisfy this condition***.

Hence, the missing number is **57**.

**__Method II__:**

Each term of the given series can be expressed as ***"a² - (a - 1)**"* as shown below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/210238f6b45a32d14d0b06eb70dc32be4eec1370ac3491da1fefdbdda9dcf3b9.png] 

 
• Here, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 are consecutive even numbers in ascending order.
 
• Similarly, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 are consecutive odd numbers in ascending order.

Among the given options, ***only 57 can satisfy this condition***.

Hence, the missing number is **57**.

questions.question:
Two statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows from the statements.

**Statements:**

All ponds are pools.

Some wells are ponds.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some ponds are not wells.

II. Some wells are pools.

III. All pools are wells.
questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b3581e07b9c39b68df7a962c821187e2f61f147818e575bbb850c06718e3ffb.png] 

I. Some ponds are not wells → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. Some wells are pools → True (Some wells are ponds and all ponds are pools)

III. All pools are wells → False (It is possible but not definite)

Hence, only conclusion II follows.

questions.question:
Select the number pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as the two numbers of the pair given below.

35 : 6
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

(n² - 1) : n

1) 85 : 9 → does not follow the rule as 9² – 1 = 80 ≠ 85

2) **120 : 11 → follow the rule as 11² – 1 = 120**

3) 26 : 5 → does not follow the rule as 5² – 1 = 24 ≠ 26

4) 64 : 8 → does not follow the rule as 8² – 1 = 63 ≠ 64

Hence, 120 : 11 is the correct answer.
